name: Snowflake
scope_notes: Avoid treating default PAT safeguards as immutable. Verify client/driver and cloud support for federation.

controls.name: Authentication policy AUTHENTICATION_METHODS
controls.what: Allow-list of auth methods; omitting PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN, KEYPAIR, WORKLOAD_IDENTITY or OAUTH blocks that method for the account or user.
controls.setting: CREATE/ALTER AUTHENTICATION POLICY ... AUTHENTICATION_METHODS; ALTER ACCOUNT/USER SET AUTHENTICATION POLICY
controls.quote: PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN: Allows users to authenticate with a programmatic access token.

controls.name: Authentication policy SECURITY_INTEGRATIONS
controls.what: Limits which SAML/OIDC/External OAuth security integrations can be used.
controls.quote: A list of security integrations the authentication policy is associated with.

controls.name: PAT_POLICY MAX_EXPIRY_IN_DAYS / DEFAULT_EXPIRY_IN_DAYS
controls.what: Sets the default (15 days) and maximum (365 days) PAT lifetime; lowering the max breaks longer existing tokens.
controls.quote: Specifies the maximum number of days that can be set for the expiration time for a programmatic access token.

controls.name: PAT network policy requirement (NETWORK_POLICY_EVALUATION)
controls.what: By default a user must be subject to a network policy to create or use PATs; admins can relax this.
controls.quote: the user must be subject to a network policy with one or more network rules to generate or use programmatic access tokens

controls.name: PAT role restriction requirement
controls.what: Service-user PATs must name a single role by default; admins can also require it for person users.
controls.quote: you must specify the role that will be used during sessions authenticated with that token.

controls.name: MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS privilege
controls.what: Only roles with OWNERSHIP or this privilege on a user can manage that user's PATs, key pairs or workload identities.
controls.setting: GRANT MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS ON USER ... TO ROLE
controls.quote: you must use a role that has the OWNERSHIP or MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS privilege on that user.

controls.name: Disable / revoke PAT
controls.what: Admins can disable or remove a PAT; disabling a user's login disables their PATs.
controls.setting: ALTER USER ... MODIFY / REMOVE PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKEN
controls.quote: You cannot recover a programmatic access token after you revoke it.

controls.name: Network policies (account / user / security integration)
controls.what: Restrict inbound access by IP or private endpoint; integration-level policy overrides user and account policies.
controls.setting: CREATE NETWORK POLICY; ALTER ACCOUNT/USER/SECURITY INTEGRATION SET NETWORK_POLICY
controls.quote: the most specific network policy overrides more general network policies.

controls.name: Snowflake OAuth integration ENABLED
controls.setting: ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION ... SET ENABLED = FALSE
controls.quote: Specifies whether to initiate operation of the integration or suspend it.

controls.name: OAUTH_ISSUE_REFRESH_TOKENS / OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_VALIDITY
controls.what: Turns refresh tokens off or sets their validity (custom clients 1 to 90 days, default 90).

controls.name: OAUTH_SINGLE_USE_REFRESH_TOKENS_REQUIRED
controls.what: Requires refresh tokens to be single-use.
controls.quote: Specifies whether single-use refresh tokens should be used.

controls.name: OAUTH_ENFORCE_PKCE
controls.what: Requires PKCE for every authorization instead of only when the client sends it.
controls.quote: we highly recommend that your client require PKCE for all authorizations.

controls.name: External OAuth integration ENABLED
controls.setting: ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION ... SET ENABLED = FALSE
controls.quote: `FALSE` suspends the integration for maintenance. Any integration between Snowflake and a third-party service fails to work.

controls.name: EXTERNAL_OAUTH_ANY_ROLE_MODE
controls.what: When DISABLE (default), clients cannot switch to roles beyond those in the token.
controls.quote: `DISABLE` does not allow the OAuth client or user to switch roles.

controls.name: EXTERNAL_OAUTH_ISSUER / EXTERNAL_OAUTH_AUDIENCE_LIST
controls.what: Only tokens from the configured issuer and audience values are accepted.
controls.quote: Specifies additional values for the access token’s audience validation.

controls.name: Named key pairs (role restriction and expiration)
controls.what: Keys added with ADD KEY PAIR can carry a role restriction and expiry; legacy RSA_PUBLIC_KEY cannot.
controls.setting: ALTER USER ... ADD KEY PAIR / REMOVE KEY PAIR
controls.quote: This approach does not support role restriction or expiration.

controls.name: EXPIRE_ROTATED_KEY_PAIR_AFTER_HOURS
controls.what: Sets how long a rotated named key stays valid (default 24 hours, 0 = immediate).
controls.quote: By default, the prior key remains valid for 24 hours.

controls.name: WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_POLICY (ALLOWED_PROVIDERS / ALLOWED_AWS_ACCOUNTS / ALLOWED_AZURE_ISSUERS / ALLOWED_OIDC_ISSUERS)
controls.what: Restricts WIF to chosen providers, AWS accounts, Entra tenants or OIDC issuers.
controls.quote: Specifies the list of AWS account IDs allowed by the authentication policy during workload identity authentication of type AWS.

controls.name: Disable named workload identity
controls.what: Disables one workload identity on a service user.

controls_unknown: Edition requirements for authentication policies are not stated on the reference pages.
Whether Snowflake OAuth (as opposed to External OAuth) can be disallowed via AUTHENTICATION_METHODS; the OAUTH value is documented as 'Allows External OAuth'.
No account-wide policy found to force named key pairs or cap key-pair lifetime; legacy RSA_PUBLIC_KEY keys never expire.
Docs differ on how to unblock privileged roles for custom OAuth clients (account parameter vs Snowflake Support).
Whether the WIF quote 'disable it' covers the DEFAULT identity (docs say DEFAULT must use SET/UNSET WORKLOAD_IDENTITY).

containment.steps: Identify owner of a found secret with SELECT SYSTEM$DECODE_PAT('<secret>'); run ALTER USER <u> REMOVE PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKEN <name> (or MODIFY … SET DISABLED = TRUE to preserve for review). For wider compromise, ALTER USER <u> SET DISABLED = TRUE, which aborts running queries and disables the user's PATs.
containment.notes: Docs do not say whether sessions opened with a PAT end on removal. ALTER USER SET DISABLED = TRUE aborts running queries. Removed PATs drop out of CREDENTIALS, so snapshot the row before removing.

authentication.summary: OAuth 2.0 with Snowflake as the authorization server. A partner or custom client sends the user through Snowflake sign-in and consent, then presents the short-lived Snowflake access token; refresh tokens are optional.

federation.details: Snowflake issues the tokens itself; no external token is exchanged. Tokens from an external authorization server use External OAuth (snowflake-5), and cloud workload identities use workload identity federation (snowflake-4).

ip_restriction.boundary: A network policy on the Snowflake OAuth integration covers code exchange, refresh token use and access token use, and overrides user and account policies. User-level policies are not checked on token requests (except the built-in local-application integration).

lifetime.summary: Default 10 min; configurable 1 min–1 h per integration

renewal.summary: Refresh tokens (on by default) default to 90 days (7776000 s); custom clients allow 1–90 days and partner apps 1 h–90 days, then the user must re-authorize. Single-use refresh tokens are optional.

administration.summary: Roles with CREATE INTEGRATION (ACCOUNTADMIN by default) create the integration. ACCOUNTADMIN, ORGADMIN, GLOBALORGADMIN and SECURITYADMIN are blocked by default; BLOCKED_ROLES_LIST, refresh-token settings and an integration network policy are set per integration.
administration.conditions: Avoid treating default PAT safeguards as immutable. Verify client/driver and cloud support for federation.

offboard.details: OAuth sessions run as a Snowflake user. Disabling that user, which SCIM deactivation does, aborts the user's queries and blocks new logins.

token_format.notes: RS256 JWT signed by the user's private key; iss = ACCOUNT.USER.SHA256:<public_key_fingerprint>, sub = ACCOUNT.USER; valid at most 1 hour. The long-lived secret is the RSA private key (PEM), which has no Snowflake-specific prefix.

authentication.summary: An external authorization server (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, PingFederate or a custom server) issues the access token, and the client presents it to Snowflake. Snowflake validates it against the External OAuth security integration (issuer, keys, audience) and maps a token claim to a Snowflake user.

federation.details: Snowflake accepts tokens issued by the customer's own OAuth server. Trust is set per integration by issuer, signing keys (JWKS URL or RSA public key) and audience.

ip_restriction.boundary: Network policy on the External OAuth integration overrides user and account policies; logged-in sessions from blocked origins cannot run further queries. Older Entra ID and Okta setup pages still say integration-level policies are not supported and to use account-level policies, so verify in the tenant.

lifetime.summary: Set by the external authorization server; Snowflake rejects tokens past exp

renewal.summary: The client gets a new access token from the external authorization server (for example with that server's refresh token or client credentials); Snowflake issues no refresh token for this path.

administration.summary: Roles with CREATE INTEGRATION (ACCOUNTADMIN by default) create the integration. Privileged roles are blocked by default; role switching is off by default (EXTERNAL_OAUTH_ANY_ROLE_MODE). Authentication policies can allow or disallow External OAuth (OAUTH) and limit which integrations apply.
administration.conditions: Token lifetime, refresh and client grant types are controlled in the external IdP, not Snowflake. Some setup pages conflict with the network-policy page on integration-level policies.

sso.details: Tokens come from the customer's authorization server, so its MFA, subnet and approval policies apply when the token is issued.

offboard.details: The token maps to a Snowflake user. Disabling that user, which SCIM deactivation does, blocks logins and aborts the user's queries. Disabling the user in the IdP also stops new tokens.

disable.cli: SQL: ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION <name> SET ENABLED = FALSE; or AUTHENTICATION_METHODS without 'OAUTH' + ALTER ACCOUNT|USER <name> SET AUTHENTICATION POLICY <policy>

sso.ui: IdP side (Okta example): Admin Console > Security > API > Authorization Servers > (server) > Access Policies
sso.cli: SQL: token tied to user via EXTERNAL_OAUTH_ISSUER and EXTERNAL_OAUTH_TOKEN_USER_MAPPING_CLAIM on the integration

network.cli: SQL: ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION <name> SET NETWORK_POLICY = '<np>'

expiry.ui: Okta: Security > API > Authorization Servers > (server) > Access Policies > Add Rule > 'Access token lifetime is'

token_format.notes: JWT issued by the external IdP (Okta, Entra ID, Ping, custom); format set by the IdP. Must carry session:role scopes and the user-mapping claim (e.g. sub, upn).

containment.steps: Revoke tokens/sessions and disable the user at the IdP; ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION <int> SET ENABLED = FALSE for issuer compromise; ALTER USER <u> SET DISABLED = TRUE to abort running queries and block login.
containment.notes: Snowflake validates IdP tokens locally; docs do not describe revoking an IdP-issued token in Snowflake, so issued tokens may stay usable until expiry unless the user or integration is disabled.

sample_query.query: SELECT s.session_id, s.user_name, l.client_ip, l.authorizing_integration_name, q.role_name, q.query_text FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY l JOIN SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.SESSIONS s ON s.login_event_id = l.event_id JOIN SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY q ON q.session_id = s.session_id WHERE l.first_authentication_factor = 'OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN' AND l.authorizing_integration_name = 'OKTA_EXT_OAUTH' AND l.client_ip = '203.0.113.24';
